title: Kodak Invented the Digital Camera, Then Hid It

scenes.say: Remember Kodak film? The company that ruled photography for almost a century invented the digital camera. And then it hid it.
December 1975. A young Kodak engineer named Steve Sasson builds the world's first digital camera. It weighs about eight pounds.
It takes black and white photos of just ten thousand pixels, and needs twenty three seconds to save each one to a cassette tape.
Sasson shows it to Kodak's bosses. He later said their reaction was: that's cute, but don't tell anyone about it.
Why hide it? Because film was a gold mine. In 1976, Kodak sold around ninety percent of all film in America.
So Kodak protected film. Rivals built the digital cameras. Then phones put a camera in every pocket.
Three months later, a photo sharing app with just thirteen employees is bought for one billion dollars.
scenes.sub: for a photo app with 13 employees

scenes.say: Here is the lesson. Kodak did not miss the future. It saw it first, and chose to protect what was already making money.
So ask yourself. In your career or your business, what are you protecting that might be holding you back?
